declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Config;

/**
 * Which analyzer implementation builds the dependency graph.
 *
 * The kinds are closed, so every place that reacts to the choice — the use case
 * that constructs the analyzer above all — has to name an arm for each of them,
 * and adding a third analyzer is reported at every such place instead of falling
 * through a default.
 */
enum AnalyzerKind: string
{
    /** Builds the graph from real sources, using PHPStan to resolve types */
    case PhpStan = 'phpstan';

    /** Builds the same graph from real sources, reading them directly instead of through PHPStan */
    case Native = 'native';

    /** Builds a synthetic graph, for exercising output without parsing sources */
    case Debug = 'debug';
}

## Analyzers

Two analyzers read real sources, and they are built to describe the same graph:

| `--type`  | What it does | Where it is available |
|-----------|--------------|-----------------------|
| `phpstan` | Runs PHPStan over the sources and assembles the graph from what its collectors report. The reference engine. | Installed from source or via Composer |
| `native`  | Reads the sources directly with a parser, resolving names the way PHP does. Between 13x and 59x faster. | Everywhere, including the released PHAR |

```bash
peq 'App\Domain\Invoice::total' src --type=native
```

**The released PHAR carries only `native`.** Bundling a static analyser to run a parser
is most of the download for none of the answers: the PHAR is 7.2MB where PHPStan alone
is 47MB. `--type` there offers `native|debug` and refuses anything else — the choice a
build can make is the choice it is asked to make. Installed from source or via Composer,
`--type=phpstan` is there and remains the default.

The two are not asked to agree by inspection. `native` is checked against `phpstan` by
comparing the graphs they build of the same sources, reduced to a canonical form: a
corpus of scenarios written to exercise every kind of symbol and relation the graph
model has, peq's own sources, and programs drawn at random by a property test that
shrinks any disagreement to the one expression that causes it.

with both engines and fails on any difference, so a package that arrives tomorrow is read
tomorrow:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Tests\Equivalence;

use App\Analyzer\AnalysisFailedException;
use App\Analyzer\Graph\GraphSnapshot;
use App\Analyzer\NativeAnalyzer\NativeAnalyzer;
use App\Analyzer\PhpStanAnalyzer\PhpStanAnalyzer;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\CoversNothing;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Large;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\RunTestsInSeparateProcesses;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use Tests\Fixture\Analyzer\InstalledPackages;

/**
 * @internal
 */
#[CoversNothing]
#[Large]
#[RunTestsInSeparateProcesses]
final class InstalledPackageEquivalenceTest extends TestCase
{
    /**
     * @param string $package The name of the installed package
     * @param string $path    The source tree it keeps its code in
     *
     * @throws AnalysisFailedException If the reference engine cannot finish reading the package
     */
    #[DataProvider('providerInstalledPackages')]
    public function testBothEnginesDescribeTheSameGraphOfRealCode(string $package, string $path): void
    {
        $reference = GraphSnapshot::of((new PhpStanAnalyzer())->analyze($path));
        $candidate = GraphSnapshot::of((new NativeAnalyzer())->analyze($path));

        self::assertNotSame([], $reference->nodes, $package.' gives the engines nothing to disagree about');
        self::assertSame($reference->fingerprint(), $candidate->fingerprint(), $package.': '.$candidate->differenceFrom($reference)->describe());
    }

    /**
     * @return iterable<string, array{string, string}>
     */
    public static function providerInstalledPackages(): iterable
    {
        foreach (InstalledPackages::sourceRoots(dirname(__DIR__, 2)) as $package => $path) {
            yield $package => [$package, $path];
        }
    }

cd /Users/ab/Projects/peq-native-engine && cat > /tmp/peq-probe/commit2.txt <<'MSG'
Ship a binary that carries one engine, and check the other in CI

Three things the review asked for.

The architecture layers now cover the new engine. deptrac had no layer for
src/Analyzer/NativeAnalyzer, so its boundaries were unenforced while reporting
zero violations; it may now depend on Analyzer and Graph, and the use case may
depend on it, which is what PhpStanAnalyzer already had.

The distributed binary carries only the engine that reads sources directly.
phpstan/phpstan moves to require-dev and nikic/php-parser — which the new
engine needs and which was only ever present as a development dependency —
moves to require. The PHAR drops from bundling a 47MB static analyser to 7.2MB
in total. Being absent is not enough on its own: a kind whose engine is not
installed is now neither offered nor accepted, so --type in the PHAR reads
"native|debug" and refuses anything else, while a checkout or a Composer
install still offers phpstan and still defaults to it. AnalyzerKind says what
each kind is built on and answers whether it is installed; RawConfig reads the
field against the kinds that can be chosen rather than the kinds that exist.

The guarantee runs in CI. The contract and integration checks already ran
there under composer test on five PHP versions, and the property test under
the property-based workflow; what was missing was the real-world sweep that
found the abstract-trait-method rule in the first place. It is now a test that
reads every installed dependency with both engines — thirty-four packages
today, and whatever arrives tomorrow — in its own workflow. It lives outside
every testsuite in phpunit.xml.dist on purpose, so neither composer test nor
the mutation run pays for it, and each package runs in a process of its own:
the reference engine keeps what it reflected over, and thirty-odd whole-package
analyses in one process come to nearly two gigabytes, where one process each
holds fourteen megabytes and the sweep takes two minutes.

The build job now checks what it built: that the PHAR carries no PHPStan file,
that it offers only the engines it carries and refuses the one it does not,
and that it still reads a source tree.

The README loses a requirement on ext-ast that nothing in the project has ever
asked for, which a binary this size should not claim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## Follow-up: deptrac layer, PHAR without PHPStan, and the guarantee in CI

### 1. deptrac now covers the new engine

```yaml
    - name: NativeAnalyzer
      collectors:
        - type: directory
          value: src/Analyzer/NativeAnalyzer/.*
```

`Action` may depend on it; it may depend on `Analyzer` and `Graph` — the same shape
`PhpStanAnalyzer` already had. 0 violations, and the layer is enforced rather than
merely passing.

### 2. The released PHAR carries one engine

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `phpstan/phpstan` | `require` (47MB bundled) | `require-dev`, **0 files in the PHAR** |
| `nikic/php-parser` | dev-only by accident | `require` (1.8MB) |
| PHAR size | — | **7.23MB** |
| `--type` in the PHAR | `phpstan\|native\|debug` | **`native\|debug`** |
| `--type` from source or Composer | `phpstan\|native\|debug` | unchanged, still defaults to `phpstan` |

Absence alone is not enough, so the choice is derived rather than hard-coded:
`AnalyzerKind::requires()` names the class each kind is built on, `isAvailable()`
answers whether it is installed, and `RawConfig::oneOf()` reads the field against the
kinds that can be chosen rather than the kinds that exist. In the PHAR:

```
$ ./peq.phar --help inspect | grep type
      --type=TYPE   Analyzer type (native|debug)

$ ./peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src --type=phpstan
Invalid configuration "type": expected one of native, debug, got "phpstan".   # exit 1
```

`nikic/php-parser` moving into `require` is a correction, not a new cost: the new
engine has always needed it, and it was only present because a development dependency
happened to pull it in.

### 3. The guarantee is CI

Most of it already was — this makes the rest explicit:

| Check | Where it runs |
|---|---|
| 20-scenario corpus + kind coverage (contract) | `composer test`, PHP 8.1–8.5 |
| peq's own sources (integration) | `composer test`, PHP 8.1–8.5 |
| Drawn programs with shrinking (property) | `Property-based tests` workflow, every push and PR |
| **Every installed dependency** | **`Engine equivalence` workflow** (new), every push and PR, plus weekly |
| **The PHAR is what it claims** | **`build` job** (new steps) |

The sweep reads all 34 installed packages with both engines — and whatever arrives
tomorrow, since the list is what is on disk rather than a list in a file. It takes
**2m06s** and passes.

Two constraints shaped it, both measured rather than assumed:

- It lives in `tests/Equivalence/`, which no testsuite in `phpunit.xml.dist` includes,
  so neither `composer test` nor the mutation run pays for it. That avoided needing a
  second protected-file change.
- Each package runs in its own process. The reference engine keeps what it reflected
  over: thirty-odd whole-package analyses in one process reach **1,925MB** and blow the
  suite's 2G limit, and `gc_collect_cycles()` recovers none of it. One process each
  holds 14MB and costs under a second.

The build job now checks the PHAR carries no PHPStan file, offers only the engines it
carries, refuses the one it does not, and still reads a source tree.

### Also

The README claimed peq requires `ext-ast`. Nothing in the project has ever asked for
it, and a 7MB binary should not claim a requirement it does not have, so the line is
gone.

### Checks

`composer lint` and every suite — unit, contract, integration, property, doctest,
`composer test:pbt`, `composer test:equivalence` — pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

content.text:
3点とも入れて push しました（PR #38 に追記済み、CI 実行中）。

## 1. deptrac レイヤー追加

`NativeAnalyzer` レイヤーを追加し、`Action → NativeAnalyzer`、`NativeAnalyzer → Analyzer, Graph` を許可しました（`PhpStanAnalyzer` と同じ形）。violations 0 で、境界が「通っているだけ」から「強制されている」状態になりました。

## 2. PHAR を native 専用に

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `phpstan/phpstan` | `require`（47MB 同梱） | `require-dev`、**PHAR 内 0 ファイル** |
| `nikic/php-parser` | dev 依存にたまたま存在 | `require`（1.8MB） |
| PHAR サイズ | — | **7.23MB** |
| PHAR の `--type` | `phpstan\|native\|debug` | **`native\|debug`** |
| ソース/Composer の `--type` | 同左 | 変更なし・既定も `phpstan` のまま |

「入っていないから動かない」ではなく、選択肢そのものを導出しています。`AnalyzerKind::requires()` が各エンジンの依存クラスを名前で示し、`isAvailable()` がインストール有無を答え、`RawConfig::oneOf()` が「型として存在する値」ではなく「選べる値」に対して検証します。

```
$ ./peq.phar --help inspect | grep type
      --type=TYPE   Analyzer type (native|debug)

$ ./peq.phar 'App\...\Graph' src --type=phpstan
Invalid configuration "type": expected one of native, debug, got "phpstan".   # exit 1
```

`nikic/php-parser` の `require` 移動は新規コストではなく修正です（native エンジンは元から必要で、dev 依存経由で偶然入っていただけです）。

## 3. 保証系の CI 化

contract / integration は既に `composer test` で PHP 8.1〜8.5 全部に乗っており、property test も専用ワークフローで動いていました。欠けていたのは**実コードの掃引**（abstract trait メソッド規則を発見した検証）なので、これを新規ワークフローにしました。

インストール済み依存 34 パッケージ全部を両エンジンで読み、差分があれば失敗します。リストはファイルではなくディスク上の実態なので、明日入る依存は明日読まれます。**2分06秒**で通ります。

設計上の制約は 2 つとも実測に基づいています:

- `tests/Equivalence/` は `phpunit.xml.dist` のどの testsuite にも属さないため、`composer test` も mutation も費用を払いません（保護ファイルの 2 回目の変更も不要になりました）。
- パッケージごとに別プロセスで実行します。参照エンジンは反射した内容を保持し続けるため、1 プロセスで 30 数回の全体解析を行うと **1,925MB** に達して 2G 上限を超えます（`gc_collect_cycles()` では 1 バイトも回収されません）。プロセス分離なら各 14MB、1 件 1 秒未満です。

加えて build ジョブが、PHAR に PHPStan のファイルが 0 であること・積んでいるエンジンしか提示しないこと・積んでいないものを拒否すること・実際にソースツリーを読めることを検証します。

## ついでに

README の `ext-ast` 要件は、プロジェクト内のどこからも要求されていないので削除しました。7MB のバイナリが持たない要件を主張すべきではないと判断しています。

---

CI の結果（新規の "Both engines over installed packages" ジョブを含む）は完了し次第お知らせします。最大 60 倍という数字は、PHPStan のキャッシュが冷えている初回では 500 倍近くまで開きます（`src` の初回が 55 秒 対 0.11 秒）が、PR には暖機後の正直な数字を載せています。

cd /Users/ab/Projects/peq-native-engine && git add -A && git status --porcelain && cat > /tmp/peq-probe/commit3.txt <<'MSG'
Restore two tests lost to an edit, and list what config now executes

The lint job caught two public methods with no test method named after
them — CallableEmitter::signature() and TraitFlattening::methodWritten().
Both had one; an edit that rewrote the tail of each test file to move its
helpers into fixtures took the tests with it. They are back, and
signature() gains the case that says it records nothing for a signature
naming only builtin types.

PHPStan did not report this locally because the rule reads across files:
its result cache had the two source files from before the test files
changed, and reused them. Clearing the result cache reproduces the job.

The runs that collect coverage — mutation testing and the docs preview —
reported twenty risky tests, all of them the same thing. Reading the
analyzer from configuration now executes AnalyzerKind, where before it
only named the class, so every test that loads a configuration touches it.
The five test classes that do now say so.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
